_comment: RT-12's declared set (bharatstudio-requirements/reviews/2026-09-16-prf-02-slice-2-scope-review.md
decision #2: 'a manifest AND a route scan. Both, not either.'). This file is the manifest half:
every app_private function that backs an overlay/widget-facing route MUST have an entry here, and
every entry MUST have a current EXPLAIN artefact (enforced by check-plans.mjs). The scan half
(scan-required-queries.mjs) finds every app_private.list_overlay_* call actually present in
apps/api/src/db/*.ts and apps/api/src/routes/*.ts and fails the build if one of them is missing
from the 'function' list below — so forgetting to add an entry here is not a silent gap, it is a
failed build. See scan-required-queries.mjs's own header for exactly what the scan does and does
not catch.
Entries here were originally the 10 RT-12 shipped (goal, challenge, hype, leaderboard, vote,
paid-vote, recent-tips, top-supporters, supporter-ticker, mega-tip-banner). Building the scan for
THIS task (closing the two PRF-02 master-canvas gaps) honestly discovered three more pre-existing
widget-backing queries with no artefact at all: list_overlay_lottie_assets and
list_overlay_widget_config (both predate PRF-02, migrations 0077/0105) and
list_channel_master_canvas_modules (creator-facing, not overlay-session-gated like the others, but
named explicitly in this task's own command as needing an artefact). A scan built to only catch the
two functions this task's authors already knew about would be the exact same failure pattern RT-12
itself exists to prevent, so all five gaps the honest general-purpose scan found are captured, not
only the two originally named. See reviews/2026-09-16-prf-02-slice-2-implementation.md and
tests/TC-RT-12-explain-plans.md (both in bharatstudio-requirements) for the full account.
2026-09-16, scan-convention-independence closure: the scan above (and this manifest) only ever
keyed on the list_overlay_* naming convention, so a same-file call to an app_private function under
any other name was invisible to it. Opus enumerated every app_private.* call in the seven dedicated
overlay-facing store files (challenge-overlay-store.ts, goal-overlay-store.ts,
master-canvas-sql-store.ts, overlay-audio-store.ts, overlay-branding-store.ts, overlay-store.ts,
overlay-wakeup.ts) and found 7 of 12 distinct functions missing -- most importantly
app_private.get_overlay_events, the alert stream itself and the single hottest overlay read in the
product, added below with its own artefact. The other six
(ack_overlay_cursor, can_access_channel, get_overlay_lottie_asset, get_overlay_tts_audio,
lookup_overlay_token, upsert_master_canvas_module) are writes, auth/predicate lookups, or
single-row byte-serving fetches by primary key -- each judged individually and exempted below with
its own reason, not swept in as a group. scan-required-queries.mjs is now convention-independent
for these seven files: it requires every app_private call inside them, any name, to be either here
or in "exemptions" below. See reviews/2026-09-16-rt-12-scan-convention-independence.md and
tests/TC-RT-12-explain-plans.md (both in bharatstudio-requirements) for the full classification
reasoning and what still can slip past the scan.
2026-09-16, scan blind-spot closure (second correction, same day). The two rules above are BOTH
naming rules -- rule 1 keys on the function name (list_overlay_*), rule 2 on the file name
(overlay / master-canvas). A store file matching NEITHER that added an overlay-facing read was
invisible to both: a green check blind to what it was never told about, which is the exact defect
RT-12 exists to prevent. scan-required-queries.mjs now also runs rule 3, which consults no name at
all. It starts at apps/api/src/index.ts and apps/api/src/app.ts, finds every call whose argument
list contains the derivedReadSql token -- the single handle to RT-10/RT-11's bounded, statement-
timeout-bearing derived-read pool, which every widget/dashboard/analytics read is required to run
on -- resolves each callee through that file's own import statements, brace-matches the named
export's body, and requires every app_private call inside that body to be here or in exemptions.
A rename cannot defeat it: the file name lives in the import specifier rule 3 follows, and the
factory name lives in both the call site and the export it matches. Rule 3 newly surfaced three
calls, all three creator-dashboard reads on the same derived-read pool, none overlay-facing:
list_channel_payments, get_channel_revenue_kpis and get_creator_activation_state -- each exempted
below with the routing and function-body evidence for that judgement, not the bare assertion. See
reviews/2026-09-16-rt-12-scan-convention-independence.md's 'Correction' section and
active/tasks/RT-12.md (both in bharatstudio-requirements).

new in PRF-02 slice 6 / PRF-06, migration 0139 -- module #5 (Reaction Cloud). All three scan rules cover this call independently: rule 1 by the list_overlay_* name, rule 2 because apps/api/src/db/reaction-cloud-overlay-store.ts matches the overlay filename rule, and rule 3 because apps/api/src/index.ts constructs createSqlReactionCloudOverlayStore with derivedReadSql. The read is SERVER-SIDE SAMPLED -- it returns catalogue entry ids and counts only, capped by the configured-but-unset display ceiling inside the function, never the reaction stream (FULL-PRODUCT-DEFINITION.md 19.5, 12.7). The WRITE path app_private.record_channel_reaction is deliberately NOT listed and needs no exemption: it is an insert on the main pool, not a derived read, so no rule reaches it -- see the artefact's own note

PRF-02 module #12 (Moderator Status Card). Introduced by migration 0136 (held half) and REDEFINED by migration 0138, which completes the module by adding the creator's safe-mode flag -- the artefact's Defined-at line and query_hash now point at 0138, because 0138 drops and re-creates the function (PostgreSQL cannot change OUT columns with create-or-replace, the same mechanic 0127 used for get_overlay_events). All three scan rules cover this call independently: rule 1 by the list_overlay_* name, rule 2 because apps/api/src/db/moderator-status-overlay-store.ts matches the overlay filename rule, and rule 3 because apps/api/src/index.ts constructs createSqlModeratorStatusOverlayStore with derivedReadSql. The read returns exactly held_count and safe_mode and nothing else -- see the artefact and packages/db/tests/prf02_slice5_moderator_status.sql's returned-column-set assertion, which was extended to the new declared type rather than deleted. The CREATOR-facing safe-mode read/write (app_private.get_channel_safe_mode / set_channel_safe_mode, migration 0138) is deliberately NOT listed here: apps/api/src/db/safe-mode-store.ts is constructed with the main sql pool rather than derivedReadSql, its basename matches neither the overlay nor the master-canvas filename rule, and its functions are not list_overlay_*, so no scan rule reaches it -- the same structural position db/stream-mission-store.ts occupies

new in PRF-02 slice 6, migration 0142 -- module #17 (Giveaway / Tournament Card), built ON module #16's lobby (migration 0140) rather than beside it (FULL-PRODUCT-DEFINITION.md 17.2). All three scan rules cover this call independently: rule 1 by the list_overlay_* name, rule 2 because apps/api/src/db/giveaway-tournament-overlay-store.ts matches the overlay filename rule, and rule 3 because apps/api/src/index.ts constructs createSqlGiveawayTournamentOverlayStore with derivedReadSql. The read returns exactly entry_count, entry_closes_at, tournament_current_round, tournament_total_rounds, tournament_completed_matches_in_round and tournament_matches_in_round and nothing else -- aggregate entry state and bracket state only, enforced on the declared result type and asserted in packages/db/tests/prf02_slice6_giveaway_tournament.sql, the same way 0136, 0139 and 0140 enforce theirs. There is NO WINNER on this path and none is possible in this slice: 17.1 permits an announcement only WITH CONSENT and no consent mechanism exists in this schema, a winner is a participant identifier on an aggregate-only path, and nothing could produce one -- the mechanic is not built (17.1, decided 2026-09-13) and GIV-07 gates chance-based formats on a legal review that has not happened and stays Blocked. There is no randomness primitive anywhere in 0142 either, asserted structurally against every shipped function definition; and no prize, escrow, custody, fulfilment, delivery, address or claim column exists, because BharatStudio never holds, escrows, ships or guarantees a prize. The bracket's field size, total rounds and matches-in-round are DERIVED at read time from the referenced public.lobby_sessions row's seat_count and are stored nowhere -- that is how 17.2's 'built on the Lobby Engine rather than beside it' is enforced rather than asserted. The 30.3 Creator+/Events-Pack entitlement is migration 0140's app_private.events_pack_entitled, CALLED from inside this function rather than reimplemented, so an unentitled channel's valid overlay token returns zero rows; the artefact captures that. The CREATOR-facing giveaway and tournament reads and writes (app_private.open_giveaway, update_giveaway_entry_count, close_giveaway, list_channel_giveaway, start_tournament, set_tournament_progress, conclude_tournament, list_channel_tournament, migration 0142) are deliberately NOT listed here: apps/api/src/db/giveaway-tournament-store.ts is constructed with the main sql pool rather than derivedReadSql, its basename matches neither the overlay nor the master-canvas filename rule, and its functions are not list_overlay_*, so no scan rule reaches them -- the same structural position db/lobby-status-store.ts, db/stream-mission-store.ts and db/safe-mode-store.ts occupy

new in PRF-02 slice 6, migration 0140 -- module #16 (Lobby Status). The read returns exactly seat_count, confirmed_seat_count and queue_count and nothing else -- FULL-PRODUCT-DEFINITION.md 16's "aggregate status only ... never player identifiers, never Discord names, never codes or passwords" is enforced on the declared result type and asserted in packages/db/tests/prf02_slice6_lobby_status.sql, the same way 0136 and 0139 enforce theirs. The 30.3 Creator+/Events-Pack entitlement is inside this function too (app_private.events_pack_entitled), so an unentitled channel's valid overlay token returns zero rows; the artefact captures that. The CREATOR-facing lobby read/writes (app_private.open_lobby_session, update_lobby_session_counts, close_lobby_session, list_channel_lobby_session, migration 0140) are deliberately NOT listed here: apps/api/src/db/lobby-status-store.ts is constructed with the main sql pool rather than derivedReadSql, its basename matches neither the overlay nor the master-canvas filename rule, and its functions are not list_overlay_*, so no scan rule reaches them -- the same structural position db/stream-mission-store.ts and db/safe-mode-store.ts occupy

new in PRF-02 slice 7, migration 0145 -- module #11 (Sponsor Card). All three scan rules cover this call independently: rule 1 by the list_overlay_* name, rule 2 because apps/api/src/db/sponsor-card-overlay-store.ts matches the overlay filename rule, and rule 3 because apps/api/src/index.ts constructs createSqlSponsorCardOverlayStore with derivedReadSql. The read returns exactly sponsor_name, logo_mime_type and logo_storage_key and nothing else -- THE CARD RENDERS THE SPONSOR AND COUNTS NOTHING (owner decision, 2026-09-17): no impression, exposure, view, duration, shown_at or displayed_at column exists anywhere in migration 0145, asserted structurally in packages/db/tests/prf02_slice7_sponsor_card.sql against every function this migration ships and against information_schema.columns, and the returned column set is separately asserted (from pg_get_function_result and from a live call materialised into a table). A row is returned ONLY when the card is enabled and, if it has a schedule, the current instant falls inside it -- both conditions are WHERE-clause predicates inside this function, not a post-filter, and the artefact demonstrates a disabled card and a card outside its window each independently producing zero rows with the same valid token. sponsor_card is already one of migration 0131's twenty Master Canvas catalogue keys and carries no second tier gate; nothing in 0145 reads a tier or calls an entitlement function. The CREATOR-facing sponsor-card read/write (app_private.upsert_sponsor_card, list_channel_sponsor_card, migration 0145) is deliberately NOT listed here: apps/api/src/db/sponsor-card-store.ts is constructed with the main sql pool rather than derivedReadSql, its basename matches neither the overlay nor the master-canvas filename rule, and its functions are not list_overlay_*, so no scan rule reaches them -- the same structural position db/stream-mission-store.ts, db/lobby-status-store.ts and db/giveaway-tournament-store.ts occupy

exemptions.reason: auth lookup, not a widget read -- validates the bearer token fingerprint against overlay_sessions and returns session/channel identity only (packages/db/migrations/0003_v1_l03_application.sql). Runs before every overlay read as an admission check (RT-02 S3.2(a)); it never returns widget-facing rows itself.

auth predicate (boolean), not a widget read -- used in the WHERE clause of creator-facing overlay-session revoke/rotate mutations in apps/api/src/db/overlay-store.ts, gating a write rather than serving overlay content.
write -- marks a delivery acknowledged and upserts the overlay's cursor row (packages/db/migrations/0022_v1_l05_overlay_ack_release.sql); returns a boolean, not widget-facing data.

write -- creator-facing module enable/disable toggle (packages/db/migrations/0131_v1_prf02_master_canvas_modules.sql), owner/admin authorized; returns the module id, not widget-facing data. The read that renders from this state, app_private.list_overlay_master_canvas_modules, already has its own manifest entry (master-canvas-modules-overlay.explain.md).

single-row byte-serving fetch by artifact primary key (packages/db/migrations/0067_v1_l03_tts_event_enrichment.sql) -- returns one TTS artifact's audio bytes for the overlay's own separate playback fetch, keyed on target_artifact_id plus a session/token re-check, not an aggregate or list a widget renders from. The read that surfaces which artifact to fetch, app_private.get_overlay_events, is manifested above.

single-row byte-serving fetch by artifact primary key (packages/db/migrations/0077_v1_l03_lottie_branding_upload.sql), same shape and same reason as get_overlay_tts_audio above -- its own comment in the migration calls it out explicitly as 'the byte-serving path ... fetches by artifact id' distinct from the enumerating list. The enumerating list it complements, app_private.list_overlay_lottie_assets, already has its own manifest entry (lottie-assets.explain.md).

creator-dashboard payment-ledger read, not an overlay read -- and 'not overlay-facing' here is a determination, not an assertion. How it was determined, three independent checks: (1) ROUTING -- apps/api/src/app.ts registers it only through registerPaymentLedgerRoutes(app, dependencies.sessions, dependencies.paymentLedger) (apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts:9), which takes the creator SessionStore; the dependency field paymentLedger is passed to no overlay registrar (registerOverlayRoutes / registerOverlayAudioRoutes / registerOverlayLottieRoutes) and to no widget route. (2) SIGNATURE AND BODY -- packages/db/migrations/0071_v1_l03_payment_ledger_read.sql:21 defines it as (target_channel_id uuid, target_cursor_created_at timestamptz, target_cursor_id uuid, target_limit integer) guarded by app_private.has_channel_role(target_channel_id, array['owner','admin']); it neither accepts an overlay id nor a token fingerprint and never joins public.overlay_sessions, which every manifested overlay read does (compare app_private.list_overlay_goal(target_overlay_id uuid, target_token_fingerprint text), 0102:365). (3) SCOPE -- active/tasks/RT-12.md's Boundaries section already excluded the payments ledger by name and assigned the dashboard/history EXPLAIN inventory to PRF-11 (FULL-PRODUCT-DEFINITION.md S31.18.1), a separate register row; manifesting it here would be the scope creep that record forbids, not extra rigour. It is visible to rule 3 only because it shares RT-10/RT-11's derived-read pool, which is what that pool is for. PRF-11, not RT-12, is where its plan artefact belongs.

creator-dashboard revenue KPI aggregate, not an overlay read -- determined the same three ways as list_channel_payments above. (1) ROUTING -- reached only via registerInsightsRoutes(app, dependencies.sessions, dependencies.insights) (apps/api/src/app.ts) serving GET /v1/channels/:channelId/revenue-kpis (apps/api/src/routes/insights.ts:49), a creator-session route; dependencies.insights reaches no overlay registrar. (2) SIGNATURE AND BODY -- packages/db/migrations/0133_v1_ops08_ops11_activation_and_revenue_kpis.sql:154 defines it as (target_channel_id uuid, window_start timestamptz, window_end timestamptz) with the migration's own ACCESS note 'financial amounts, so owner/admin only'; no overlay id, no token fingerprint, no overlay_sessions join. (3) SCOPE -- OPS-11 dashboard analytics, the surface active/tasks/RT-12.md's Boundaries assign to PRF-11 (S31.18.1). Rule 3 sees it because OPS-08/OPS-11 correctly wired it to RT-10/RT-11's derived-read pool rather than the main request pool.

creator-dashboard activation-checklist read, not an overlay read -- determined the same three ways. (1) ROUTING -- reached only via registerInsightsRoutes serving GET /v1/channels/:channelId/activation-state (apps/api/src/routes/insights.ts:30), a creator-session route; no overlay registrar receives dependencies.insights. (2) SIGNATURE AND BODY -- packages/db/migrations/0133_v1_ops08_ops11_activation_and_revenue_kpis.sql:46 defines it as (target_channel_id uuid) returning six booleans/timestamps guarded by app_private.can_access_channel; it takes no overlay id and no token fingerprint. Note it does READ overlay_connected state, which is why it must be judged rather than dismissed on its name: it reports to the CREATOR whether an overlay has ever connected, it does not serve bytes or rows to an overlay session. (3) SCOPE -- OPS-08 dashboard analytics, PRF-11 territory per active/tasks/RT-12.md's Boundaries. Visible to rule 3 because it runs on RT-10/RT-11's derived-read pool.
